conviction_note: The print turns on the guide, not the quarter: Q3 (ended 2026-09-30, before the reported 26-Oct ramp-down layoffs) faces a revenue bar of ~$84.4-85.0M that already embeds an ~8% sequential drop management flagged as possible, so a reported-quarter beat is likely (print_vs_bar +4%), but this name sells beats without a raise and the first guide under a new CEO must absorb an unquantified Q4 program ramp-down; against that sits a 37% fall since 26-Oct, ~13% of shares short and call-heavy open interest, so p_up is only 52 on a 20% absolute move and the findings net to +0.7.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue consensus ~$84.4-85.0M (Yahoo avg $84.42M from 4 analysts, FXEmpire $84.99M, Benzinga/Earnings Whispers $84.7M; https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/INOD/22312, 2026-10-28) against Q2 actual $92.1M. EPS bar disputed ($0.17-$0.27 across sources), so EPS-dependent sizing is capped. Company guide: FY2026 revenue growth 40%+ on FY2025 $251.7M = >= $352.4M; H1 = $182.2M, so H2 >= $170.2M, i.e. ~$85M a quarter (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000903651/000110465926092010/tm2621499d1_ex99-1.htm, 2026-08-06). Consensus Q3 sits right at the guide floor's run-rate.
positioning_check: FINRA short interest 4,521,023 shares at 2026-10-15 settlement (-142,806), 3.65 days to cover, ~13.1% of 34.38M shares outstanding (higher as % of float; insiders hold 11.8%); 2026-10-30 settlement not yet published, equibles model estimates ~4.74M (+4.9%) (https://equibles.com/stocks/inod/shortinterest, read 2026-11-05). Skew not available (skew_25d_vol_points null); put/call open interest 0.21 (call-heavy), straddle implies 17.81% with a 46%-of-mid ATM spread. Tape: -18.5% over 5 sessions, -38.5% over 20, -69% from the 52w high, 9% above the 52w low; realised vol 120%.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-26 Innodata India terminated ~550 employees (about 5% of the 10,107 global headcount at end-2025) with termination emails citing a 'ramp-down of the business assignment', plus undisclosed cuts in the Philippines (raters, quality experts, team leads; Reddit posts tie them to a 'MUPSL' project); the company has not confirmed or quantified it, and the stock fell ~25-28% on 2026-10-27 from $59.91 and is now $37.63. This threatens the Q4 run-rate the 40%+ FY guide needs (~$85M/quarter in H2) and the first guide (2027 or a reset 2026) on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance is the line this name trades on: +86% on 2026-05-07 when Q1 beat by 18% and the FY guide went from 35%+ to 40%+; -4.8% on 2026-08-06 when Q2 beat (+6.7% vs $86.3M) but the guide was only reiterated; -7.2% on 2026-02-26 on an initial 35%+ guide.
findings.why_not_priced: The layoff itself is fully priced: a ~37% fall (~$800M of market cap) since 2026-10-26. What is not priced either way is its size: 550 people is ~5% of the workforce against a largest customer that was 37% of Q2 revenue (~$34M/quarter); at company-average revenue per head (~$36K a year) 550 people is ~$5M a quarter, less at Indian billing rates. If the market had sized it as that small, the stock would not sit 9% off its 52w low; if it had sized it as the largest customer leaving, consensus Q3/Q4 revenue would have been cut after 26-Oct, and it sits at the same ~$84.7M Earnings Whispers carried on 28-Oct. The call is the first time management quantifies it.
findings.independence: Same event reported independently by India Today/Economic Times via Finanztrends (https://www.finanztrends.de/news/innodata-aktie-erholt-sich-nach-kurssturz/), TIKR (https://www.tikr.com/blog/innodata-sinks-28-on-reported-abrupt-layoffs-of-550-in-india-official-ids-deactivated) and People Matters for the Philippines (https://sea.peoplemattersglobal.com/news/strategic-hr/innodata-lays-off-nearly-550-employees-in-india-job-cuts-reported-in-the-philippines-53002); all rest on employee accounts and the termination email, none on a company document.

findings.finding: The Q3 revenue bar (~$84.4-85.0M, four sources) is ~8% below Q2's $92.1M because management told the Q2 call a sequential decline in Q3 or Q4 was possible ('I don't know that I would particularly care'); Q3 closed 2026-09-30, a month before the reported ramp-down, while the Q2 release said a personalization program for long-horizon agents with the largest customer was 'now scaling', a second RL-environment program had started with it, a new fast-scaling frontier lab had signed, and a Big Tech customer had gone from 17% to 34% of revenue. The reported quarter is likely to clear the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats without a raise have been sold or barely bought: Q2 2026 beat by ~6.7% and fell 4.8%; Q3 2025 beat ($62.6M vs $59.8M) and rose 6.9%; Q1 2026 beat by 18% with a raise and rose 86%. Beats alone do not carry this stock.
findings.why_not_priced: The bar was cut toward the guide-floor run-rate on management's own warning, and the post-layoff narrative has extended the ramp-down back onto the quarter that ended before it. If the market expected a clean beat of a lowered Q3 bar the stock would not have fallen another 18.5% in the five sessions to 2026-11-05 with no new company news. Inside what the company guided: a Q3 of ~$85-90M is inside the 40%+ FY path, so this is a reported-quarter item the market was told to expect, sized small.
findings.independence: Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000903651/000110465926092010/tm2621499d1_ex99-1.htm, 2026-08-06) for the programs and customer mix; Earnings Whispers preview for the bar (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/INOD/22312, 2026-10-28). Hunterbrook (long INOD) claimed on 2026-09-23 the largest customer is Meta and the personalization work supports Meta's Muse agent, launched 2026-09-08 (https://parameter.io/innodata-inod-stock-surges-15-on-speculation-of-meta-muse-partnership/) - an unconfirmed, conflicted source.

findings.finding: This is the first print under CEO Rahul Singhal (effective 2026-09-30, founder Jack Abuhoff to executive chairman) and CFO Jayant Chauhan (effective 2026-07-06), who must address an unconfirmed ramp-down on the call; a new team has an incentive to set the first 2027 framework or a reset 2026 guide conservatively.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print under this team. The last two prints with only a reiterated guide fell 4.8% and 6.9% (2026-08-06, 2026-06-17 CFO appointment plus reaffirmation).
findings.why_not_priced: Management change was public for months and the stock still traded near $60-70 into late October, so the market did not treat it as a guide risk until the layoffs; the combination (new team plus ramp-down) is what makes a conservative reset more likely, and the Earnings Whispers preview notes bearish sentiment at 37% from under 6%, so some of it is now priced.
findings.independence: CEO transition in the Q2 call/release (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2942769); Earnings Whispers notes it is the first report under the new CEO and CFO (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/INOD/22312).

findings.finding: Peer TaskUs reported on 2026-11-04 Q3 service revenue $314.7M (+5.4% y/y, record) with AI Services +28% y/y for the seventh straight quarter as its fastest-growing line, raised FY2026 revenue guidance by $20M at the midpoint, and said revenue ex its largest client grew nearly 20% (so its largest client shrank y/y).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured history of INOD reacting to TaskUs prints.
findings.why_not_priced: It landed the day before the print and after Innodata's last statement; INOD did not rally on it (it is still at the low of its five-session slide). It is a proxy: frontier-lab and AI-data demand held through Q3 at a peer, which says nothing about Innodata's specific ramp-down. The read-across on the largest-client decline is unconfirmed (neither company names it).
findings.independence: Proxy only. Appen's 2026-10-29 update (filed separately below) points the other way on volume.

findings.finding: Appen's Q3 FY26 quarterly activity report (2026-10-29) maintained FY26 revenue guidance of $270-300M but said visibility points to the lower half, while adding two US frontier model builders and saying new-account revenue would be modest in FY26.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured history of INOD reacting to Appen updates.
findings.why_not_priced: A weak, idiosyncratic peer (much of Appen's revenue is China); small read-across to AI-data vendor volumes in the second half. Public a week before the print.
findings.independence: Opposite in sign to the TaskUs finding; together they net near zero on industry demand.

findings.finding: Into the print the stock is down 37% from $59.91 (2026-10-26 close) to $37.63, -18.5% in five sessions with no new company disclosure, 9% above its 52-week low, with ~4.5M shares short (~13% of shares outstanding, 3.65 days to cover at 2026-10-15, modelled higher at 2026-10-30) and call-heavy open interest (put/call 0.21); a held FY guide or a quantified, small ramp-down has a short-covering mechanism in the window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After a 32.8% three-month slide into 2025-11-06 the stock rose 6.9% on a beat; after the 2026-05-07 setup (short interest ~17% in April 2026 per Benzinga) the stock rose 86% on a raise.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the thing the price already reflects, but the asymmetry is real: the 5-session slide to the low after the initial gap means sellers have front-run the guide; a crowded short and a 120% realised vol mean any relief is large. If the market priced a balanced outcome, the stock would not be sitting this close to the 52w low with the straddle at 17.8%.
findings.independence: Price path from MarketBeat (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-innodata-nasdaq-inod-shares-gap-down-heres-why-2026-10-27/) and the sealed baseline; short interest from equibles (FINRA data).

findings.finding: The Q2 10-Q shows advances from customers of $67.0M at 2026-06-30 (from $1.8M at year-end) for unfulfilled obligations, with $61.8M of incurred-but-unpaid project costs in payables, and states revenue includes reimbursement of out-of-pocket (pass-through) expenses; the release put customer prepayments for pass-through costs at ~$116M within $250.4M of cash. Recognition of pass-through work in Q3/Q4 could lift reported revenue against the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No history on pass-through revenue; the market did not react to it at the Q2 print.
findings.why_not_priced: Inference from a footnote: no preview mentions the prepayment build or its recognition timing; pass-through revenue is low-margin, so it would help the revenue line more than EPS, and a sophisticated reader may discount it.
findings.independence: Same company filing family as the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000903651/000110465926092010/tm2621499d1_ex99-1.htm); Panabee summary repeats the $116M figure (https://www.panabee.com/news/innodata-earnings-q2-2026).

findings.finding: On 2026-08-06 Innodata put a $300M at-the-market equity program in place (Goldman, Craig-Hallum, Wells Fargo, Maxim, Wedbush; reference price $70.21) under an automatic shelf, with ~$134M of net cash and no stated use; with the stock now near $38 any Q3 sales disclosed in the 10-Q, or continued use, dilutes at a much lower price.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Filed with the Q2 print, which fell 4.8%; not separable.
findings.why_not_priced: The program is public; whether shares were sold in Q3 (when the stock was $50-70) is not, and it appears in the 10-Q filed with the print. What the money buys: no corroborated use beyond general growth (the company already held $134M net cash and $116M of customer prepayments), so it is neither a funded-ramp positive nor distress; sized near zero.

findings.finding: Director Louise Forlenza sold 10,000 shares at an average $53.54 ($535K) on 2026-09-14, cutting her holding 64.8% to 5,424 shares; no other open-market insider sale since, and the October Form 4 is a director RSU grant.
findings.why_not_priced: Small, public, a non-executive director; mildly informative only because it preceded the ramp-down by six weeks.
findings.independence: EDGAR Form 4 index (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0000903651&type=4) shows filings 2026-09-04 and 2026-09-15 consistent with it.

outside_window.finding: FINRA short-interest settlement 2026-10-30 (publication expected 2026-11-10) will show whether shorts added into the layoff gap; resolves after the exit.

searched_and_found_nothing: Company statement, 8-K or press release on the October layoffs: none on EDGAR through 2026-10-30 (latest filings S-8 2026-10-27, SC 13G/A 2026-10-30)
Identity of the 'MUPSL' project or the client ramped down: no public source
Analyst notes after 2026-10-27 with numbers (Maxim reportedly kept Buy on 2026-11-03 per a German headline, no detail retrievable)

rejected_candidates.detail: A consequence of the layoff report in finding 1; carries no information of its own.

rejected_candidates.detail: Dated 2025 on the URL path; describes the prior-year print, not this one.

rejected_candidates.detail: Folded into finding 2's independence; the program itself comes from the Q2 release.

baseline_tension: No skew is available; the -38.5% 20-day run-up and call-heavy open interest point to sellers having front-run a guide cut, and the evidence is split - a low Q3 bar and crowded short against an unquantified Q4 ramp-down under a new team - so it neither confirms nor cuts against the drawdown.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction): Q3 reported-quarter beat cut from +1.5 to +1.0 because this name sold its last un-raised beat (-4.8% on 2026-08-06).
Lesson 7 (crowded short shrinks negatives): ~13% of shares out short, so the layoff/guidance negative went from -1.5 to -1.2 and the new-CEO reset from -1.0 to -0.8, once each.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): ATM has no corroborated use and no distress, sized from -0.3 to -0.2.
Lesson 9 and 5 left standing: the layoff finding was already sized net of the 34% Big Tech customer and new programs; TaskUs/Appen proxies kept small and filed, not dropped.
